systems.name: Bannistar Station
systems.blurb: The great fuel gantries — new-built to feed the Lamplighters' advance down the Run — and Okrent's Drift, the boomtown port that grew on their back, now in recession since the advance stalled. The frayed end of the living Duros Space Run. Its beacon, Vesta-9, was relit in 90 AR — nobody admits to lighting it.

gm.seed: Session One — The Light on Vesta-9
gm.canon: Canonically a massive refueling depot (attested in Clone Wars-era sources, 900 years later — use freely). Vesta-9 is the beacon here; certified by Chartmistress Bel Nerra (Lamplighters). GM truth: the Sith apprentice lit it.

systems.name: Enarc
systems.blurb: A sealed junction — the Enarc Run (toward Naboo and the Rimma) and the Hutt-ringed Triellus once met the Run here — now the Anchorage of Sorulba, a closed Hutt kingdom where any ship may dock and none has left in forty years. Spacers say Enarc eats ships.

gm.seed: Session Two — the Anchorage's opening crisis: the King's Circuit swoop race and the campaign's first hand-lit beacon At the festival: a dig-chandler's stall, Sund & Daughter (GM: Mendac in cover — never reveal; one tell, exact change, witnessed once per module); and the court's stuck Inheritor clerk, 'the archivist of the door'.
gm.canon: Real junction: Enarc Run + Triellus (Hutt space ring). Campaign frame: the closed hermit kingdom of Sorulba's kajidic. The door swings ONE WAY — any ship may arrive and is welcomed and absorbed; exit visas are the king's rarest grant (almost never in forty years); embassy personnel are exempt by treaty. That is why the Run knows nothing of the kingdom though the junction is on every old chart: nobody who found it ever came back. No toll on the lane because no traffic; its one quiet foreign relationship runs down the Enarc Run to Naboo (the Admiralty). The opening crisis begins when the guild posts the Enarc prize.

systems.name: Verdanth
systems.blurb: Jungle world.

gm.seed: The Oracle of Brel (Brel = a settlement moon here?); the swamp Del Gormo was born in — empty until the hill on Aquilaris no longer needs him (he is there in time for Yoda, 104 AR). The hermit is Kerra Holt's student, never the Temple's. The seventeen dead lords' sealed tombs; the relight brings the Vigil to seal them, first and only pass. Full detail: gm/npcs/knight-errant.md. GM: the Inheritors' capital — Lord Vhasla's sealed temple, its nameplate chiseled away (the stolen name defaced at the source); the Unveiling is shown to the crew privately inside, and the culling triggers after they leave. Odri's counter sets up outside the temple. Module 05 (The Seventeen Tombs; play order 03 → 05 → 04): seventeen clearings visible from the beacon ridge — sixteen under Vigil tape, one (the temple) lit and untaped; the beacon relay is a Republic mast on the ridge above the old landing field, the easy relight; the Unbroken Seal runs at a tomb the crew chooses; the Emptied House is the temple itself, found when the landing-field band goes silent; Vhasla's necrology date is 1029 BBY.
gm.canon: Jungle world; otherwise blank.

systems.name: Brel
systems.blurb: Brel — a settlement moon of Verdanth; a small farming community with a shrine.

gm.seed: The Oracle of Brel — Anwei, ten, an Awakened child whose true dreams are eating her sleep, worshipped by the settlement and guarded by its armed faithful; courted by three factions the same week the crew arrives (the Inheritors, the Vigil, the crew — module 05, Scene 3); her prophecy 'don't go in the second door' points at the Verdanth temple's bare vault. Stats: gm/npcs/reaches.md.
gm.canon: Campaign-invented moon of Verdanth (no Legends source).

systems.name: Aplooine
systems.blurb: An ash-drowned world: ash to three hundred meters, nothing breathable below the weathered peaks. Life holds on in sealed peak-holds, and ash-drivers cross the moving Sea for pay.

gm.seed: Module 04 (The Ash Sea): the beacon mast was swallowed by a slide two generations ago — three meters still showing (“the Snorkel”); a thirteen-thousand-year-old Kymoodon colony hulk the ash surfaced this season; sealed peak-holds and the ash-drivers.
gm.canon: Legends (Treece's survey): ash to 300 m, no breathable atmosphere, landing points only on weathered peaks; inhabited since the Kymoodon Era — one of this pocket's two seed-worlds.

systems.name: Sanrafsix
systems.blurb: The great dead hub — its bazaars thrived on the last war's economy and died with it. Junction of the smugglers' Sanrafsix Corridor.

gm.canon: Great dead trade hub of the New Sith Wars economy — provenance bazaars fit perfectly. Don't crater it: alive in later-era sources. Legends: a cosmopolitan hub whose groundside population was sealed in and lost to the Candorian plague in the wars' last century while the orbital stations lived — the Memory Market is an orbital bazaar above a dead, sealed city. The article names its Run links as Aplooine and Heptooine — the hop order as drawn.

systems.name: Heptooine
systems.blurb: The Run's last waystop.

gm.canon: Route stop.

systems.name: Jutrand
systems.blurb: City-planet; capital of a dead Sith principality, haunted by its own grandeur.

gm.seed: The Sealed Enclave or The Dead Letter
gm.canon: Ex-Bactranate capital — haunted grandeur. Inherit the Knight Errant (1032 BBY) state.

systems.name: Darkknell
systems.blurb: The lights come back on: a trinary-sun trade city that never stopped, the Hydian Way's local anchor.

gm.canon: Never went dark. 'An important trading center for millennia,' trinary suns. The dark closes around it, never through it. The Sanctum Celestial — Daiman's heptagonal fortress in Xakrea — is a Force vergence (F&D Core Rulebook; flooded in the Battle of Darkknell, 1032 BBY).

systems.name: Eriadu
systems.blurb: One Hydian hop south: an old, modest world of shellwork jewelry sitting on the most valuable crossroads in the southern Rim — the Hydian Way, the Rimma Trade Route and the minor Lipsec Run. Rumors of coreward money.

gm.canon: At 910 BBY modest and ancient. The Quintad (Corulag oligarch families) canonically arrive ~900 BBY. The crew's relit corridor is part of why the money comes.

systems.name: Fostin Nine
systems.blurb: First stop down the Sanrafsix Corridor, a notorious smugglers' road.

gm.canon: Sanrafsix Corridor.

systems.name: Syned
systems.blurb: Corridor waypoint.

gm.canon: Sanrafsix Corridor.

systems.name: Omwat
systems.blurb: The Corridor runs on past here into Hutt-adjacent space.

gm.canon: Sanrafsix Corridor.

systems.name: Veshet
systems.blurb: A settlement off a dead spur of the Corridor.

gm.canon: Off a dead spur of the Sanrafsix Corridor; the dead withdrawn lineage's four unmarked graves are here.

systems.name: Chelloa
systems.blurb: A dead principality spur. Baradium-scarred.

gm.canon: Devastated in Knight Errant (1032 BBY). Floor, not ceiling.

systems.name: Byllura
systems.blurb: A dead principality spur.

gm.seed: The Last Muster (suggested placement, GM-placeable) — Kaan's dead man's switch: a working of Sith magic bound into Dyarchy stonework over the cache that holds his record (the Kaan holocron) and the Brotherhood's reserve, firing since the thought bomb cut his thread. The grinding call the gifted hear up the Run is this switch relaying the Valley; the Banite line is deaf to it. Off every catalogue — the crew reaches it by walking the call, not by chart. See Keepers of the Flame.
gm.canon: The Dyarchy fell here (Knight Errant) — the Dyarchy's world, where for a decade a whole population moved to the will of two telepath children; stonework that remembers obedience is exactly the Brotherhood's kind of irony. Last Muster placement per Keepers of the Flame.

systems.name: Aquilaris
systems.blurb: Drowned resort world — oceans over old pleasure piers; first of the deep-Reach stops.

gm.seed: Kerra Holt's birthplace and grave — the sisters' stone on Tarrah Hill, the planet's highest point (HOLT / Marenna / Kerra / Sisters, cut by Del Gormo), her green lightsaber (first ignition in a player's hand or not at all) and the undelivered recorder beneath. Del Gormo LIVES here, keeper of his master's grave; he has tolerated the Vigil's tape for ninety years because a tended grave is a safe one. Set piece: The Hill on Aquilaris, on the relight — the truce breaks (the wardens stop tending and start sealing: a manifest, not a tape); two claimants only, the Vigil vs Del Gormo. Full scene: gm/npcs/knight-errant.md. Module 03 (The Drowned Resort): the beacon mast is the Grand Pier tower, half a kilometer out in the bay, top third above water — and it was never dead: the Seacroppers diverted its power to the harvester stations' life support for sixty years, so relighting it darkens the refugee road (the session's price). Capital Cay is the Seacroppers' town on the roofs of a Republic port; the Deep hunts at dusk, on a schedule. The Inheritors' introduction: a produced rescue on the water and a testimony commission — the warm knock (module 03). Odri's beat here: a rooftop counter on Capital Cay, Sund & Daughter, buying salvage off the drowned promenades.
gm.canon: Legends: aquatic resort world (Aquilaris, Sanbra sector). Knight Errant-era Grumani neighbour; promoted onto the Run at its atlas position.

systems.name: Gazzari
systems.blurb: A dead principality spur — an old battlefield.

gm.canon: Knight Errant battlefield.

systems.name: Naboo
systems.blurb: Quiet, half-charted world at the far end of the Enarc Run; home of the Naboo Admiralty — the fleet that never demobilized.

gm.seed: The Naboo Admiralty — the fleet that refused the Ruusan demobilization sailed rimward down the Enarc Run (~20 AR) and fortified this pocket. Revealed only when Vesta-9 lights; NAS Steadfast arrives at Vesta-9 from INSIDE the dark Run, not the Bannistar side.
gm.canon: Legends Naboo (Chommell sector, Mid Rim), the Enarc Run's rimward endpoint. Plasma seams underwrite the Admiralty's yards. Faction crack: treaty-keepers vs the Founding.

systems.name: Triffis
systems.blurb: First living stop behind Bannistar on the Mid Rim stretch of the Run — the last prize the guild paid (85 AR), claimed by the crew of the Larksong — five years before Vesta-9 lit.

gm.canon: Transit point on the Run (The Essential Atlas).

systems.name: Kyrska
systems.blurb: Quiet world on the living Run, relit by a Lamplighter prize over 82–83 AR; reconnection has been slower to change it than its neighbors.

gm.canon: User-invented: no Legends source. Keep it a quiet foil to the boomtown stops.

systems.name: Glom Tho
systems.blurb: Mid Rim waystop on the living stretch of the Run, relit by a Lamplighter prize in 84 AR.

gm.canon: Transit point on the Run (The Essential Atlas).

systems.name: Kalarba
systems.blurb: Mid Rim world on the living stretch of the Run, relit by a Lamplighter first-lighting prize in 81 AR — the first paid on the Run.

gm.canon: Transit point on the Run (The Essential Atlas).

systems.name: Churba
systems.blurb: Where the Duros Space Run meets the Corellian Run — the far, living end of the road the crew is relighting from the other side.

gm.canon: Endpoint of the Run with New Cov; junction with the Corellian Run (The Essential Atlas).

systems.name: New Cov
systems.blurb: Churba's twin at the Run's Mid Rim end; the Corellian Run carries on coreward from here.

gm.canon: Named with Churba as the Run's endpoint. Alive in later-era sources — goes quiet, doesn't crater.

systems.name: Corellia
systems.blurb: Coreward up the Corellian Run: shipwrights, smugglers, and the Republic's other great artery.

gm.canon: Off-chart context arrow — the Corellian Run's coreward reach.

systems.name: Bonadan
systems.blurb: The Hydian runs on past Brentaal to its far northern terminus among the money worlds.

gm.canon: Off-chart context arrow — the Hydian's northern end.

systems.name: Fondor
systems.blurb: The Rimma Trade Route crosses the Hydian at Eriadu and runs coreward toward the great yards.

gm.canon: Off-chart context arrow — the Rimma's coreward branch at the Eriadu junction.

systems.name: Sluis Van
systems.blurb: The Rimma's rimward branch, off the Eriadu crossroads toward the southern yards.

gm.canon: Off-chart context arrow — the Rimma's rimward branch.

systems.name: Terminus

gm.canon: Off-chart context arrow — the Hydian's southern end.

systems.name: Quermia
systems.blurb: The Perlemian carries on past Lantillies toward its far end.

gm.canon: Off-chart context arrow — the Perlemian's far end.

systems.name: Malastare
systems.blurb: A raw colony barely older than the dark years, coreward on the Hydian.

gm.canon: ~90-year-old Gran colony among Dug natives — a mirror of the era, not an established power.

systems.name: Denon
systems.blurb: Hydian Way, coreward.

gm.canon: Hydian waypoint.

systems.name: Brentaal
systems.blurb: Where the Hydian crosses the Perlemian Trade Route.

gm.canon: Hydian × Perlemian junction.

systems.name: Lantillies
systems.blurb: Rimward down the Perlemian; the Randon Run begins here.

gm.canon: Perlemian → Randon Run.

systems.name: Kashyyyk
systems.blurb: The Randon Run passes the Wookiee homeworld.

gm.canon: Randon Run waypoint.

systems.name: Teraab
systems.blurb: Off the charts: nebulae quietly eating the last lanes to Ruusan since the war ended.

gm.seed: Act 3 — the hardest astrogation of the campaign; fragments are the only charts.
gm.canon: The Valley is a 'lost world' by 11 BBY.

systems.name: Ruusan
systems.blurb: Every child knows the armies reached Ruusan seven times, so the road exists.

gm.canon: Valley of the Jedi.

systems.name: Coruscant
systems.blurb: The capital, a hop or two coreward of Brentaal on the Perlemian. When the Republic's recovery money finally comes back out to the Rim, this is the road it takes.

gm.canon: Coruscant is on the Perlemian Trade Route, not the Hydian; Brentaal is the junction. The Reformation's appropriations stopped here — the dark years are this road going quiet.
